title: bOPEN Program Goal and Measurable Outcomes v0.2 Requirement Catalog

source.title: bOPEN Program Goal and Measurable Outcomes v0.2

items.normalized_statement: Establish a secure, reusable, governed multi-tenant business platform kernel for multiple BST products, capabilities, and industry modules without rebuilding common platform foundations.
Maintain traceable human and agent accountability.

By P4, demonstrate that a new multi-tenant product or module can be registered, specified, implemented, verified, activated, and operated without rebuilding the platform kernel or weakening tenant isolation.
Certified Module Enablement Rate equals modules reaching pilot through the standard bOPEN module lifecycle divided by total modules submitted for pilot, multiplied by 100.
Certified Module Enablement Rate target for P2.
Certified Module Enablement Rate target for P3.
items.target: At least 3 certified shared foundation modules

items.normalized_statement: Certified Module Enablement Rate target for P4.
items.target: At least 1 complete product composition and 5 certified modules

items.normalized_statement: Certified Module Enablement Rate target for Post-P4.
items.target: ≥90% of eligible modules reach pilot without platform-kernel modification

items.normalized_statement: Module has an approved module contract.
Module has registered permissions and entitlements.
Ensure every material change is authorized, traceable, independently reviewed, and supported by reproducible evidence.
Work items are linked to approved requirements.
Material work items have an assigned maker and checker.
Work items execute in registered branches or worktrees.
Accepted work items have evidence envelopes.
Architecture-impacting changes are linked to an ADR.
Implementation completion requires traceability, independent verification, and evidence; code or passing tests alone are insufficient.
Prevent one tenant from accessing, modifying, referencing, or inferring another tenant's protected data or resources.
Tenant-aware tables have an approved tenant key.
Tenant-aware tables are protected by verified RLS or stronger isolation.
Cache, file, search, and export isolation tests pass.
Missing or invalid tenant-context tests deny.
Critical or high unresolved isolation findings at release.
A release is blocked when a mandatory tenant-isolation control fails, is skipped without approval, or lacks reproducible evidence.
Implement shared platform capabilities once and make them reusable by all BST products.
Products use the canonical principal model.
Products use the common authorization layer.
Products use the common audit and event foundation.
Industry-specific logic introduced into the platform kernel without approval.
Shared capabilities have defined owners and contracts.
Product teams extend bOPEN through modules and registered interfaces instead of modifying the kernel for product-specific behavior.
Reduce the time, risk, and variability required to deliver new modules.
Modules have documented APIs and events.
Modules have registered permissions and entitlements.
One repeatable delivery pipeline governs every module from registration through pilot.
Use bPro to prove the platform through a complete real product workflow.
Verify another tenant cannot access the result
Complete reference flow is successfully executed.
Tenant-isolation cases for the reference flow pass.
Outbox delivery completes without data inconsistency.
Portal restricted and not-entitled states are implemented.
Critical reference-flow defects at P4 exit.
High-severity unresolved defects at pilot decision.
bPro proves the platform contract without product-specific shortcuts.
Ensure bOPEN can be monitored, supported, restored, and safely rolled back.
Required logs, traces, and metrics are available.
Unresolved high vulnerabilities without approved treatment.
P95 interactive API latency for standard non-analytical operations.
Revise initial service targets using measured production and pilot evidence.
Use approved agent harnesses to increase delivery capacity without fragmenting authority or compromising quality.
Active agents are recorded in the agent registry.
Agent tasks have bounded repository scope.
Agent sessions are linked to work-item IDs.
Material agent changes are independently reviewed.
Structured handoffs meet the handoff contract.
Agent-produced claims are supported by evidence.
Agents independently authorize their own release.
Conflicting concurrent mutations to the same controlled files.
Accepted work completed per delivery cycle
Percentage of agent-generated changes requiring major rework
Parallel workstreams completed without integration conflict
Human review time saved without reducing control coverage
Do not measure productivity only by generated code volume.
Convert verified implementation and operational experience into durable institutional knowledge.
Verified lessons are linked to corrective actions.
Promoted skills have sandbox and evaluation evidence.
Skills have named owners and review dates.
Expired or failing skills remaining active.
Repeated defects with previously verified root causes.
Reuse of approved patterns and skills.
Raw model memory, session summaries, and unsupported agent conclusions do not become governing knowledge automatically.
Agent, goal, module, skill, and schedule registers are established.
Work-item and evidence templates are operational.
Repository and CI controls are demonstrated.
A principal and tenant skeleton is demonstrated.
An active tenant context proof is demonstrated.
A PostgreSQL RLS proof is demonstrated.
A module registry skeleton is demonstrated.
Audit and outbox foundations are demonstrated.
Complete evidence exists for every P0 work package.
Tenant and membership lifecycles are demonstrated.
Capability, permission, and entitlement registries are demonstrated.
The module enablement lifecycle is demonstrated.
Event and interface contracts are demonstrated.
At least one certified module is demonstrated.
A shared reusable Party foundation is demonstrated.
A shared reusable Organization foundation is demonstrated.
A shared reusable Location foundation is demonstrated.
A shared reusable Document foundation is demonstrated.
A shared reusable Asset foundation is demonstrated.
A shared reusable Money foundation is demonstrated.
A shared reusable Measurement foundation is demonstrated.
A shared reusable Classification foundation is demonstrated.
Shared reusable Approval and notification foundations are demonstrated.
The complete bPro reference flow is demonstrated.
Independent conformance covers audit and outbox.
A control counts as passed only when reproducible evidence exists.
Skipped tests do not count as passed.
Partially implemented modules do not count as certified.
An agent-generated report is not independent verification when the same agent implemented the change.
A release delivered on time but failing a mandatory gate is unsuccessful.
Productivity improvements do not reduce test, security, evidence, or review coverage.
Targets are re-baselined when actual measurement shows the estimate is unrealistic.
Every re-baseline preserves the intended control outcome and is formally recorded.
Deliver products and modules with less duplicated platform development.
Deliver products and modules with faster controlled module onboarding.
Deliver products and modules with verified tenant isolation.
Deliver products and modules with consistent security and authorization.
Deliver products and modules with complete traceability and evidence.
Deliver products and modules with reliable operations and recovery.
Deliver products and modules with reusable architecture, knowledge, and skills.
Program success is not merely completion of bOPEN source code.
Establish a repeatable digital-product operating capability for safely governing multiple industry platforms at increasing scale.
